what: Hasbro makes toys and games. Its most valuable business by far is Wizards of the Coast, which owns Magic: The Gathering and Dungeons and Dragons, alongside traditional toy brands such as Nerf, Play-Doh, Transformers and Monopoly.
customers: Retailers selling toys and games, game players buying cards directly, and licensees using its characters.
money: Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming
Magic: The Gathering, Dungeons and Dragons and licensed video games
Nerf, Play-Doh, Transformers and other toys
moat: Magic: The Gathering, a thirty-year-old card game with a dedicated player base and a secondary market, which no competitor has successfully displaced.
risks: Toy revenue has been shrinking and the segment earns little
Revenue has fallen about 7% a year over three years
Tariffs raise the cost of toys manufactured in Asia
opportunities: Revenue grew about 13% last year, led by Wizards of the Coast
Gross margin of 76% reflects the card game's economics
Licensed collaborations have expanded Magic's audience substantially
watch: Wizards of the Coast revenue and whether the toy business stabilises.
